messages:
mike: Heads up — we rolled nvidia driver 550 to the us-west GPU pool and ~8 nodes are dropping into an initramfs drop/boot loop. Not customer-facing yet but internal batch jobs are failing.
anya: ugh. any logs from the failed boots?
mike: paste logs / dkms output: 
```
DKMS make.log for nvidia-550/550.10 (kernel 6.1.0-25-generic x86_64)
ERROR: could not locate kernel headers for 6.1.0-25-generic
modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/6.1.0-25-generic
```
jia: sounds like the driver package is trying to build kernel modules via DKMS but the kernel headers aren't present on the image. did the image pipeline bump kernels?
mike: looks like it. some nodes had auto-upgrade to 6.1 while the nvidia package in our rollout expects headers that were only packaged for 5.15 variants. we pushed the driver as a unified apt package (nvidia-driver-550) so DKMS kicks in.
oliver: cordoning affected nodes now: gpu-uw1-03, gpu-uw1-05, gpu-uw1-07..10 — cordon + drain started :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: gpu-uw1-05 cordoned by oliver at 2026-03-18T10:05:12Z
anya: quick checklist — either we: (A) boot back to previous kernel and reinstall driver so DKMS builds against the matching headers, or (B) reimage the nodes with the correct kernel-headers baked into the image. reimage is faster to get them back in production but loses ephemeral state.
mike: confirmed. nodes with initramfs loops will need reimage to recover quickly. for others we can boot to the old kernel and reinstall.
jia: workaround commands for manual recovery (tested on a dev node):
```
sudo apt-get install --reinstall linux-headers-5.15.0-50-generic dkms nvidia-driver-550 -y
sudo update-initramfs -u -k 5.15.0-50-generic
sudo reboot
```
anya: i'm pausing the driver rollout to other regions. keeping a hold on the rollout artifact while we patch the image builder to ensure kernel-headers are always included and DKMS preinstalled.
mike: rolling back the rollout now for any remaining queued hosts in us-west. also adding a guard in the rollout job to verify `dkms status` and `ls /lib/modules/$(uname -r)` before proceeding.
oliver: cost/ops note — reimaging 8 GPUs is ~3 GPU-hours each while they reprovision; ballpark $80–140 depending on instance type. tagging infra-costs.
jia: also flagging potential NCCL/library mismatch risk: if driver and cuda runtime mismatch across nodes you can see hangs in distributed jobs (socket timeouts, NCCL WARN). add a smoke test that runs `nvidia-smi`, `nvcc --version`, and a small NCCL allreduce on one node after any driver change.
mike: agreed. i'll open an incident tracker and a runbook. incident INC-2026-004 created, linking here and setting priority P2.
ops-bot: rollback job started for nvidia-driver-550 in us-west at 2026-03-18T10:12:03Z
anya: action items: 1) patch image builder to pin matching kernel+headers and install dkms by default, 2) add rollout pre-checks (dkms, /lib/modules), 3) add smoke test for NCCL/torch, 4) reimage the 8 affected nodes. i'll take 1+2. jia — can you own 3?
jia: on it, i'll create a CI job that runs on one target node and posts results to this thread.
mike: thanks all. will post recovery updates as nodes come back.
